purpose: Independent source and argument review of The Words He Would Not Hear

sources.checked_locus: Complete §§1–5, especially §§3–4; NPNF I.10 historical English transcription.
sources.outcome: The king gives remission beyond the requested delay; the second servant repeats the first plea; refusal makes received freedom an instrument of cruelty. Judgment and heartfelt pardon remain essential.

sources.checked_locus: Complete §§1–8; especially §§1–2,7–8; NPNF I.6 historical English transcription.
sources.outcome: The hearer is both debtor and creditor; gentle words can hide an unforgiving heart; inward pardon is compatible with correction directed to another’s good. The speech does not prescribe Augustine’s ancient disciplinary methods.

sources.checked_locus: Exposition of 6:9–13 and complete Moral section, with adjacent editorial notes; NPNF I.13 historical English transcription.
sources.outcome: The heavenly Master rules masters and servants, and spiritual resistance redirects hostility from the human persecutor. The speech does not adopt the disputed heavenly-places or evil-day interpretations.

sources.checked_locus: Complete articles 1–4, including objections and replies; controlling homily loci a.1 answer/replies and a.2 answer; Dominican English, second revised edition 1920.
sources.outcome: Pardon is real and cannot be retroactively undone by a later human act; new mortal sin brings new culpability, aggravated by contempt of mercy. The speech attributes the technical distinction to Aquinas.

sources.checked_locus: Printed p.181, surrounding Offertory/Secret/Communion/Postcommunion discussion; OCR compared with a newly rendered scan of p.181/PDF197.
sources.outcome: The Secret seeks restoration through the Eucharistic sacrifice; the Postcommunion binds mind, heart and will to Christ. The homily does not adopt Schuster’s distinct present-judgment interpretation of the Communion.
Both pleas and “And he would not” match the cited witness. The causal order and final warning govern the argument.
Enemy, armor, and Gospel-of-peace claims stay within the appointed lesson; prayer in verse 18 is not imported as appointed text.
Job is upright before his losses and bodily affliction. The pastoral distinction between pain and culpable refusal is a warranted application.
The request for judgment and help under persecution supports the Communion application without presenting the Bible comparator as a translation of the adapted chant.

sources.checked_locus: Printed pp.414–415 / PDF495–496, newly separated and rendered; Collect, Epistle, Gospel, Offertory, Secret, Communion, Postcommunion.
sources.outcome: All claims about the selected appointed texts agree with the images. The Collect asks continuing protection and good works; the Secret names the willed propitiatory/restoring offering; the Postcommunion asks inward pursuit of what the mouth received.

sources.checked_locus: Printed p.181 / PDF197, newly separated and rendered.
sources.outcome: The exact printed Secret and Postcommunion paragraphs corroborate the adopted OCR and its page locator.

boundaries: Only the stated loci were checked; whole-volume hashes establish identity, not whole-volume reading.
Historical English transcriptions were checked as the identified witnesses; no fresh NPNF or Aquinas print collation was performed.
No appointment from another calendar family was used. The homily selects the base Sunday texts and makes no conditional mission or St Luke branch claim.
